question_text: Verbal Intelligence: Pen : Write :: Knife : ?
explanation: Cut. A pen is used to write; a knife is used to cut (tool : function).

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: Foot : Shoe :: Hand : ?
explanation: Glove. A shoe covers the foot; a glove covers the hand (body part : covering).

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: Doctor : Patient :: Lawyer : ?
explanation: Client. A doctor serves a patient; a lawyer serves a client (professional : person served).

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: Thermometer : Temperature :: Barometer : ?
explanation: Atmospheric pressure. Instrument : quantity it measures. A barometer measures air pressure.

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: Soldier : Army :: Sailor : ?
explanation: Navy. A soldier serves in the army; a sailor serves in the navy (member : service).

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: Famine : Food :: Drought : ?
explanation: Water. Famine is extreme shortage of food; drought is extreme shortage of water (rain).

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: Verbose : Concise :: Lavish : ?
explanation: Frugal. Both pairs are antonyms. Verbose (wordy) is opposite to concise; lavish (extravagant) is opposite to frugal (thrifty).

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: Anemometer : Wind speed :: Seismograph : ?
explanation: Earthquakes. Instrument : what it measures. A seismograph records earthquake (seismic) waves.

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: A is the brother of B. B is the sister of C. C is the father of D. How is A related to D?
explanation: Uncle. A and C are brothers (B is their sister). D is C's child, so A is D's uncle.

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: A man introduces a woman as the wife of the only son of his mother. How is the woman related to the man?
explanation: His wife. The only son of his mother is the man himself. So the woman is his wife.

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: Pointing to a man, a woman says, "He is the son of my mother's only son." How is the man related to the woman?
explanation: Nephew. Her mother's only son is her brother; the man is the brother's son, so her nephew.

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: Ali says, "Ahmed's mother is the only daughter of my mother." How is Ali related to Ahmed?
explanation: Maternal uncle. The only daughter of Ali's mother is Ali's sister. She is Ahmed's mother, so Ali is Ahmed's mother's brother: maternal uncle.

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: P is the brother of Q. Q is the sister of R. R is the mother of S. How is P related to S?
explanation: Maternal uncle. P and R are siblings (brother and sister). S is R's child, so P is S's mother's brother: maternal uncle.

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: Pointing to a girl, Bilal says, "She is the daughter of the only son of my father's father." How is the girl related to Bilal?
explanation: Sister. The only son of Bilal's father's father is Bilal's own father. His daughter is Bilal's sister.

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: A man walks 3 km east and then 4 km north. How far is he from his starting point?
explanation: 5 km. Straight-line distance = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 km.

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: A boy facing north turns right, then left, then left. Which direction is he facing now?
explanation: West. North → (right) East → (left) North → (left) West.

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: A man walks 10 m south, turns left and walks 10 m, then turns left again and walks 10 m. Where is he with respect to his starting point?
explanation: 10 m east. South 10 m puts him at (0, −10). Left from south is east: (10, −10). Left from east is north: (10, 0), i.e. 10 m east of the start.

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: One morning Ali stands facing the sun. Which direction is his left hand pointing?
explanation: North. In the morning the sun is in the east, so he faces east. Left of east is north.

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: A man walks 6 km north, then 8 km east, then 6 km south. How far and in which direction is he from the start?
explanation: 8 km east. The north and south legs cancel, leaving 8 km east.

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: A starts from a point and goes 4 km west, turns right and goes 3 km, turns right and goes 4 km, then turns left and goes 2 km. How far and in which direction is he from the start?
explanation: 5 km north. West 4 km: (−4, 0). Right (north) 3 km: (−4, 3). Right (east) 4 km: (0, 3). Left (north) 2 km: (0, 5). So 5 km due north.

explanation: 29th. Rank from bottom = total − rank from top + 1 = 40 − 12 + 1 = 29.

explanation: B. Order (tallest to shortest): A > B > C > D. The second tallest is B.

explanation: S. Age order (oldest to youngest): P > Q > R > S > T. Second youngest is S.

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: A student ranks 15th from the top and 20th from the bottom in a class. How many students are there in the class?
explanation: 34. Total = 15 + 20 − 1 = 34 (the student is counted in both ranks).

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: In a queue of 25 persons, Ali is 8th from the front and Bilal is 12th from the back. How many persons stand between them?
explanation: 5. Bilal is 25 − 12 + 1 = 14th from the front. Persons between = 14 − 8 − 1 = 5.

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: Statements: All soldiers are brave. Some brave persons are young. Conclusions: I. Some soldiers are young. II. All brave persons are soldiers.
explanation: Neither conclusion follows. From 'some brave are young' we cannot say the young ones are soldiers, and 'all soldiers are brave' does not reverse to 'all brave are soldiers'. Neither follows.

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: Statements: All cats are animals. All animals are living beings. Conclusions: I. All cats are living beings. II. All living beings are cats.
explanation: Only conclusion I follows. Cats ⊂ animals ⊂ living beings, so I follows; the reverse (II) does not.

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: Statements: Some pens are books. All books are tables. Conclusions: I. Some pens are tables. II. All tables are books.
explanation: Only conclusion I follows. The pens that are books are also tables, so I follows. Not every table need be a book, so II does not.

question_text: Verbal Intelligence: Statements: All doctors are educated. Some educated persons are rich. Conclusions: I. Some doctors are rich. II. Some rich persons are educated.
option_d: Neither conclusion follows Clock and Calendar
explanation: Only conclusion II follows. 'Some educated are rich' converts to 'some rich are educated' (II follows). The rich educated persons may not be doctors, so I does not follow.

explanation: 8,611 m. K2 is about 8,611 m (second highest in the world). 8,849 m is Everest; 8,126 m is Nanga Parbat.

explanation: The Muslim League and the Indian National Congress. Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims; Jinnah played the key role.

explanation: 1929. Announced in March 1929 as a reply to the Nehru Report (1928).

question_text: Pakistan Studies: The Allahabad Address (1930) was delivered by
explanation: Allama Muhammad Iqbal. Iqbal, as President of the Muslim League session at Allahabad (December 1930), proposed a consolidated Muslim state in north-west India.

question_text: Pakistan Studies: The Nehru Report was published in
explanation: 1928. The Nehru Report (August 1928) rejected separate electorates; Jinnah's Fourteen Points answered it.

question_text: Pakistan Studies: The Muslim League observed the 'Day of Deliverance' on

question_text: Pakistan Studies: The Cripps Mission came to India in

explanation: Indus. Tarbela (KP) is on the Indus; Mangla is on the Jhelum.

question_text: Pakistan Studies: The Durand Line Agreement between British India and Afghanistan was signed in
explanation: 1893. Signed in 1893 by Sir Mortimer Durand and Amir Abdur Rahman Khan. (1879 = Treaty of Gandamak; 1919 = Rawalpindi.)

question_text: Physics: The SI unit of pressure is
explanation: Pascal. Pressure = force/area; 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

Physics: Resistors of 6 Ω and 3 Ω are connected in parallel. Their equivalent resistance is
explanation: 2 Ω. 1/R = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2, so R = 2 Ω. (Parallel resistance is always less than the smallest.)

Physics: A transformer has 100 turns in the primary and 500 turns in the secondary. If the primary voltage is 220 V, the secondary voltage is
explanation: 1100 V. Vs/Vp = Ns/Np → Vs = 220 × 500/100 = 1100 V (a step-up transformer).

question_text: English: Choose the word closest in meaning to CANDID.
explanation: Frank. Candid = honest and straightforward.

question_text: English: Choose the word closest in meaning to OBSTINATE.
explanation: Stubborn. Obstinate = refusing to change one's opinion; stubborn.

question_text: English: Choose the word closest in meaning to ALLEVIATE.
explanation: Relieve. To alleviate pain is to make it less severe.

question_text: English: Choose the word closest in meaning to LUCID.
explanation: Clear. Lucid = clearly expressed and easy to understand.

question_text: English: Choose the word closest in meaning to PERNICIOUS.
explanation: Harmful. Pernicious = having a harmful effect, often gradually.

question_text: English: Choose the word closest in meaning to ENIGMA.
explanation: Puzzle. An enigma is a mystery or puzzling person or thing.

question_text: English: Choose the word closest in meaning to OBSEQUIOUS.
explanation: Servile. Obsequious = excessively eager to please or obey; servile, fawning.

question_text: English: Choose the word opposite in meaning to ANCIENT.
explanation: Modern. Ancient (very old) is opposite to modern.

question_text: English: Choose the word opposite in meaning to DILIGENT.
explanation: Lazy. Diligent = hardworking; its opposite is lazy (indolent).

question_text: English: Choose the word opposite in meaning to BENIGN.
explanation: Malignant. Benign (harmless, favourable) is opposite to malignant (harmful, dangerous).

question_text: English: Choose the word opposite in meaning to EXTOL.
explanation: Criticize. Extol = praise highly; the opposite is to criticize or condemn.

question_text: English: Choose the word opposite in meaning to PARSIMONIOUS.
explanation: Generous. Parsimonious = extremely unwilling to spend; opposite is generous (lavish).

question_text: English: One word for: a person who cannot be corrected.
explanation: Incorrigible. Incorrigible = too fixed in bad habits to be reformed. Incorruptible = cannot be bribed.

question_text: English: One word for: a speech delivered without preparation.
explanation: Extempore. Extempore = spoken or done without preparation. A soliloquy is a speech to oneself.

question_text: English: One word for: a place where bees are kept.
explanation: Apiary. Apiary = bees; aviary = birds; aquarium = fish.

question_text: English: What does the idiom 'to beat about the bush' mean?
option_d: To avoid coming to the point
explanation: To avoid coming to the point. It means to talk around a subject instead of addressing it directly.

question_text: English: What does the idiom 'to hit the nail on the head' mean?
option_c: To say or do exactly the right thing
explanation: To say or do exactly the right thing. It means to describe a situation or problem exactly.

question_text: English: What does the idiom 'a white elephant' mean?
option_a: A costly possession of little use
explanation: A costly possession of little use. A white elephant is something expensive to maintain but useless.

question_text: English: What does the idiom 'to smell a rat' mean?
option_b: To suspect that something is wrong
explanation: To suspect that something is wrong. It means to sense that there is trickery or something dishonest.

question_text: English: What does the idiom 'to throw in the towel' mean?
option_a: To admit defeat and give up
explanation: To admit defeat and give up. From boxing: a trainer throws in a towel to stop a fight.

question_text: English: Choose the correct option: Each of the students ____ a prize.
explanation: has received. 'Each' is singular, so it takes a singular verb: has received.

question_text: English: Choose the correct option: He insisted ____ paying the bill.
explanation: on. Insist on (doing something).

question_text: English: Choose the correct option: Hardly had he arrived ____ it began to rain.
explanation: when. Hardly/scarcely are followed by 'when'; 'no sooner' is followed by 'than'.

question_text: English: Choose the correct option: I wish I ____ a bird.
explanation: were. After 'wish' (an unreal present wish) the subjunctive 'were' is used for all persons.

question_text: English: Choose the correct option: This is the man ____ I met yesterday.
explanation: whom. 'Whom' is the object of 'met' and refers to a person.

question_text: English: Choose the correct option: Scarcely had the bell rung ____ the students ran out.
explanation: when. Scarcely/hardly ... when; no sooner ... than.

question_text: English: Choose the correct option: Neither the teacher nor the students ____ present.
explanation: were. With 'neither ... nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('students', plural): were.

question_text: English: Select the correctly spelled word.
explanation: Embarrassment. Double r and double s: embarrassment.

question_text: English: Select the correctly spelled word.
explanation: Necessary. One c, two s: necessary (one collar, two sleeves).

question_text: English: Choose the correct passive form of: 'Open the door.'
explanation: Let the door be opened.. Imperative sentences take 'Let ... be + past participle' in the passive.

question_text: General Knowledge: The largest planet in the solar system is
explanation: Jupiter. Jupiter is the largest planet.

question_text: General Knowledge: The largest ocean of the world is the
explanation: Pacific Ocean. The Pacific covers about one-third of the Earth's surface.

question_text: General Knowledge: The chemical symbol of gold is
explanation: Au. Au (from Latin aurum). Ag is silver.

question_text: General Knowledge: The smallest country of the world by area is
explanation: Vatican City. Vatican City covers about 0.44 sq km.

question_text: General Knowledge: The national animal of Pakistan is the
explanation: Markhor. The markhor (a wild goat of the mountains) is Pakistan's national animal.

question_text: General Knowledge: The Pakistan Military Academy (PMA) is located at
explanation: Kakul (Abbottabad). PMA Kakul is near Abbottabad, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

question_text: General Knowledge: Defence Day of Pakistan is observed on
explanation: 6 September. It commemorates the defence of Pakistan in the 1965 war.

question_text: General Knowledge: The first recipient of the Nishan-e-Haider was Shaheed
explanation: Captain Raja Muhammad Sarwar Shaheed. Captain Sarwar (Kashmir, 1948) was the first recipient of Pakistan's highest military gallantry award.

question_text: General Knowledge: Youm-e-Takbeer commemorates Pakistan's nuclear tests at Chagai, conducted on
explanation: 28 May 1998. Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests at Chagai (Balochistan) on 28 May 1998.

question_text: General Knowledge: The United Nations was founded in
explanation: 1945. The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945.

question_text: General Knowledge: Pakistan became a member of the United Nations on
explanation: 30 September 1947. Pakistan was admitted to the UN on 30 September 1947.

question_text: General Knowledge: The headquarters of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) is in
explanation: Jeddah. The OIC Secretariat is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

question_text: General Knowledge: The SAARC Secretariat is located in
explanation: Kathmandu. SAARC's secretariat is in Kathmandu, Nepal.

question_text: General Knowledge: The headquarters of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) is in
explanation: Tehran. ECO's secretariat is in Tehran, Iran.

question_text: General Knowledge: The motto of the Pakistan Army is
explanation: Iman, Taqwa, Jihad fi Sabilillah. 'Unity, Faith, Discipline' is the national motto; the Army's is Iman, Taqwa, Jihad fi Sabilillah.

question_text: General Knowledge: The Strait of Gibraltar separates Spain from
explanation: Morocco. The strait lies between southern Spain and northern Morocco, linking the Atlantic and the Mediterranean.

question_text: General Knowledge: Dr Abdus Salam received the Nobel Prize in Physics in
explanation: 1979. He shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics (electroweak theory).

question_text: General Knowledge: Mount Everest lies on the border of Nepal and
explanation: China (Tibet). Everest is on the Nepal-China border.

question_text: General Knowledge: NATO was established in
explanation: 1949. The North Atlantic Treaty was signed in April 1949. (1955 = Warsaw Pact.)

question_text: General Knowledge: The largest country of the world by area is
explanation: Russia. Russia covers about 17 million sq km.

question_text: Islamic Studies: Which Surah of the Holy Quran does NOT begin with Bismillah?
explanation: At-Tawbah. Surah At-Tawbah (Bara'at) is the only Surah without Bismillah at its start.

question_text: Islamic Studies: About how many Muslims fought in the Battle of Badr?
explanation: 313. About 313 Muslims faced roughly 1,000 of Quraysh on 17 Ramadan, 2 AH.

question_text: Islamic Studies: The Battle of Uhud was fought in
explanation: 3 AH. Badr 2 AH, Uhud 3 AH, Khandaq 5 AH, Hudaybiyyah 6 AH.

question_text: Islamic Studies: The idea of digging a trench (Khandaq) was suggested by
explanation: Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA). Salman al-Farsi proposed the trench in the Battle of the Trench (5 AH).

question_text: Islamic Studies: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was signed in
explanation: 6 AH. A ten-year truce with Quraysh in 6 AH, called a clear victory in Surah Al-Fath.

question_text: Islamic Studies: The expedition of Tabuk took place in
explanation: 9 AH. Tabuk was the last major expedition of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), in 9 AH.

question_text: Islamic Studies: Hazrat Umar (RA) was martyred by
explanation: Abu Lulu Firoz. Umar (RA) was stabbed in 23 AH while leading Fajr prayer. Ibn Muljam killed Hazrat Ali (RA).

question_text: Islamic Studies: Hazrat Uthman (RA) was martyred in
explanation: 35 AH. He was martyred in 35 AH (656 CE) in Madinah.

question_text: Islamic Studies: Who was appointed by Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) to head the compilation of the Quran into one volume?
explanation: Hazrat Zaid bin Thabit (RA). After the Battle of Yamamah, Zaid ibn Thabit compiled the Quran. Uthman (RA) later made standard copies.

question_text: Islamic Studies: During the Hijrah the Holy Prophet (PBUH) stayed in the Cave of Thawr for about
explanation: three days. He and Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) hid in Thawr for about three days before travelling to Madinah.
